answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so voting weight depends on reachable, independently attested paths rather than identities alone. A sybil cluster may coordinate internally, but sparse external edges give it low conductance; min-cut and transitivity bounds limit how much walk probability can flow into it, bounding its aggregate influence. Lotus, zephyr, and dawn are example node labels, not sources of extra trust.
